LEARNING UNDER THE NIGHT SKY: STUDENT EXPERIENCES OF CAMPUS STUDY SPACES

A thesis submitted in partial fulfillment of the requirements for the degree of Bachelor of Arts

Boston University 2026

Chapter 2. Methods

We interviewed four undergraduates about where they study at night. [PARTICIPANT_03], a senior who identifies as Gray mouse lemur, is majoring in Clockmaking: Technology with a second major in Orchard Management: Technology and transferred from another college. [PARTICIPANT_05] is a first-year majoring in Tea Sciences: Policy who identifies as Ring-tailed lemur. [PARTICIPANT_07] is a first-year majoring in Lighthouse Engineering: Methods who identifies as Diademed sifaka. [PARTICIPANT_09], a senior majoring in Wayfinding: Studio, identifies as Aye-aye and transferred from another college.

Chapter 3. Findings

Most participants preferred quiet spaces after 10 PM. [PARTICIPANT_03] described the library basement as the only place that felt calm during exam weeks, while [PARTICIPANT_09] studied in the transfer-student lounge between classes.

Appendix B. Interview Logistics

Interview scheduling was handled by [PERSON_01] ([EMAIL_01], [PHONE_01]). [PERSON_01] also transcribed the recordings.
